source.title: Revisiting Generalization Power of a DNN in Terms of Symbolic Interactions
source.authors: Lei Cheng; Jun-Peng Zhang; Qi-Han Ren; Quan-Shi Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests a conceptual account of generalization using interaction distributions and their similarity across training and test samples, rather than directly testing the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports interaction-distribution and training/test interaction-similarity results. It does not test the listed versions' random-label capacity, width, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal-of-memorized-examples claims.
record.test_reason: The study measures symbolic-interaction distributions and training/test interaction similarity, without testing any listed version. Its small fractions of randomized labels do not establish V1's random-label fitting comparison; parameter-noise experiments do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that generalizable interactions usually follow decay-shaped distributions and non-generalizable interactions usually follow spindle-shaped distributions, and that their fitted decomposition matches measured distributions. They explicitly restrict this to an aggregate trend, without guaranteeing the generalizability of individual interactions.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes symbolic interaction distributions and does not reproduce the original methods or interventions underlying the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise magnitude changes the reported significance of spindle-shaped distributions; the text also reports different interaction dynamics for BERT-Medium in the first phase.

fits_no_version.finding: Interaction distributions are predominantly decay-shaped at the end of normal learning; overfitting adds spindle-shaped distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Symbolic-interaction strength distributions vary systematically with learning phase in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter noise and adversarial input perturbations produce spindle-shaped interaction differences, increasingly prominent with stronger perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected perturbations produce characteristic interaction-order distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Training/test interaction-distribution Jaccard similarity decreases with interaction order.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-order symbolic interactions have greater training/test distribution similarity than high-order interactions.

record.problems: The key distribution results are mostly shown in figures without numerical values in the text. The authors state that their theory describes a general trend and cannot determine whether every individual interaction in either distribution is generalizable.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes, strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note. Testing a different account of generalization does not itself test V1–V8. Here, cannot_determine describes the rows' inability to establish these versions, not uncertainty about the reported interaction patterns.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance.
Large versus small batch held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against other measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG-11 on CIFAR-10; VGG-16 on CUB200-2011; AlexNet on CUB200-2011 and Tiny-ImageNet; BERT-Medium on SST-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured interaction strength by order across training timepoints; distributions at the end of normal learning were described as decay-shaped.
rows.measure: Distribution of positive and negative interaction strengths over orders
rows.value: The DNN mainly encoded interactions of a decay-shaped distribution at the end of the normal learning phase.
rows.note: Results are described across the listed model-dataset settings; the paper calls this partial verification of its hypothesis. This measure does not directly establish any listed version.
rows.check: Interaction-order distributions cannot establish any listed version. The condition should disclose label randomization: Appendix I.1 reports 1% on MNIST/CIFAR-10 and 5% on CUB200-2011. Figure 2 shows AlexNet on CUB200-2011; the additional Tiny-ImageNet pairing is inconsistently documented in the text.

rows.subject: VGG-11 on CIFAR-10; VGG-16 on CUB200-2011; AlexNet on CUB200-2011 and Tiny-ImageNet; BERT-Medium on SST-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured the distribution of newly emerged interactions relative to the end of normal learning.
rows.measure: Distribution of newly emerged positive and negative interaction strengths over orders
rows.value: Newly emerged interactions followed spindle-shaped distributions over orders.
rows.note: The paper describes the result as partial verification that non-generalizable representations are encoded as spindle-shaped interactions; this is not a listed claim version.
rows.check: Overfitting-associated interaction distributions cannot establish any listed version. The label-noise condition should be recorded. Figure 2 shows AlexNet on CUB200-2011; the additional Tiny-ImageNet pairing is inconsistently documented.

rows.subject: ResNet-20 on MNIST; VGG-11 on CIFAR-10; VGG-16 on CUB200-2011
rows.stage_stated: well-trained, then revised with parameter noise
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to network parameters and measured newly emerged interactions.
rows.measure: Distribution of newly emerged interaction strengths over orders
rows.value: Newly emerged interactions followed spindle-shaped distributions; the significance of spindle-shaped distributions increased with stronger noise.
rows.note: The paper does not provide numerical distribution values in the text.
rows.check: Gaussian parameter noise is assessed through interaction distributions, without magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training-error thresholds, or generalization-gap rankings required for V7. Increased 'significance' describes the distribution's prominence; no statistical significance test is reported.

rows.subject: ResNet-20 on MNIST; VGG-11 on CIFAR-10; VGG-16 on CUB200-2011
rows.stage_stated: well-trained, then evaluated on adversarially perturbed samples
rows.operation_detail: Added FGSM adversarial perturbations to samples and measured newly emerged interactions.
rows.measure: Distribution of newly emerged interaction strengths over orders
rows.value: Newly emerged interactions followed spindle-shaped distributions; the significance increased with stronger perturbations.
rows.note: The paper does not provide numerical distribution values in the text.
rows.check: Input-perturbation effects on interaction distributions do not measure any listed version. Increased 'significance' should not imply a reported statistical significance test.

rows.subject: LeNet on MNIST and Tiny-ImageNet; VGG-11 on CIFAR-10; VGG-13 on CUB200-2011
rows.operation_detail: Compared distributions of interactions extracted from training and testing samples using Jaccard similarity.
rows.measure: Jaccard similarity between training-sample and testing-sample interaction distributions
rows.value: Jaccard similarity decreased as interaction order increased; low-order interactions had higher similarity than high-order interactions.
rows.note: The paper reports a direction of change but no numerical values in the text.
rows.check: Training/test Jaccard similarity of interactions is a different construct from the held-out performance comparisons and interventions named in V1–V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
